unite_adi: UPPER SECONDARY-PREP YEAR-LEVEL: A2 - THEME 1: SCHOOL LIFE

bolumler.ogrenmeKanitlari: PERFORMANCE ASSIGNMENT: They write and design a school drama play on the content of ''school life with school rules, roles and responsibilities, activities and events at school'' including target vocabulary, grammar, and social language expressions and then they present it and perform it as a show in class by inviting other students as actors, directors, etc. The assignment will be evaluated by using rubrics. Öğrenme-Öğretme Yaşantıları
bolumler.temelKabuller: This theme includes the concept of ''school life with its components such as school rules, events, and activities at school; people, roles and responsibilities at school; national days and celebrations'' and it is assumed that it could be present in almost all languages, with some exceptions. It is assumed that a student in the preparatory year of an upper secondary school may know school life with its components such as school rules, events, and activities at school; people, roles and responsibilities at school; national days and celebrations mean in their own language as it is known that almost all people who start to learn a new language bring their pre-existing knowledge (in their own language) with them and transfer it to their new language learning context. However, they may not know how to say these things in another language if this has not yet been covered in their existing curriculum. Fortunately, this existing knowledge in their own language can help them recognise, understand, and learn them more easily in a foreign language, in this case English. As they are students in the preparatory year of an upper secondary school, they are expected to know some basic vocabulary about ''school life'' in English from previous themes and/or years such as ''an instructor, a teacher, a headmaster, to go to school and so on'' and also some structures such as ''I have to pass an English test. Students mustn’t drop litter during school celebrations. The students decorate the hall for drama performance'' in English from the previous themes and/or years. These grammar items and vocabulary are revised during the ''Revision Programme'' at the beginning of the year and they can be used as a basis for learning the new vocabulary and grammatical items in the current theme, so that the new grammatical elements in the current theme can be learnt easily.
bolumler.onDegerlendirme: It is assumed that these students in the preparatory year of an upper secondary school are ready to learn the concept of ''school rules, roles and responsibilities, activities and events at school'' cognitively, affectively, and socially since it is appropriate to their age and language level. Therefore, a contextual poster or a large picture could be provided for the students to remember and practise the items that they are related and previously learnt so that they can discuss the poster and/or the picture in pairs and write down what they remember. This session can help them revise all the related vocabulary and grammatical elements that they have already learnt from previous themes or from previous years as a preparatory practice. In this way, their performance can be evaluated in terms of how much they remember and how accurately they use these items to build their competence in the current theme. It can help the teacher decide what to emphasise, revise, and practise in order to facilitate the new vocabulary and grammatical items in the current theme. (Their performance can be evaluated by rubrics, a rating scale, and /or a marking scheme during these practices.).
bolumler.zenginlestirme: Objective: To help students to improve speaking skills in English about life at school through the creation of a poster about their ideal school with active participation by using the target vocabulary. Objective: To create a poster about their ideal school with active participation in English by using the target vocabulary. Activity 1: Design Your Ideal School Students work in pairs or groups to create their ''ideal school'' and come up with at least five school rules, explaining each rule by using modal verbs, such as ''Students mustn’t shout in the corridors'', or ''Teachers have to start lessons on time''. They brainstorm to make their rules clear and detailed. Students present their ideas using a poster or visual aid they create together and explain their rules to the class, answering questions such as ''Why must students follow this rule?''. The teacher and peers provide feedback on their clarity, fluency, and creativity, ensuring every student is engaged and contributes to the final product. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity. Objective: To help students talk about school life in English by using target social language expressions in real-life scenarios to improve their social language use in social situations, speaking fluency, and build confidence through active participation. Activity 2: Activity Name: Role-Play Scenarios The teacher writes school-related situations, such as forgetting homework or asking for permission to leave class, on pieces of paper and places them in a box. Students take turns to draw a situation from the box and act it out using expressions such as ''Chill out!'', ''Can I leave early today?'', or ''No pain, no gain!''. They actively create dialogues based on their scenario and present them to the class. After each role-play, the teacher and peers give feedback on the use of expressions, fluency, and engagement. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
bolumler.destekleme: Objective: To identify and talk about school rules in English by using target vocabulary and target grammar. Activity 1: Match and Talk The teacher prepares cards with pictures of school rules (e.g., a clean classroom, a student raising their hand) and matching phrases such as ''Keep the school tidy!'' or ''Raise your hand before speaking!''. Students match the pictures with the correct phrases using either a printed worksheet or an interactive activity displayed on a smart board or created with web 2.0 tools. For classrooms without digital tools, laminated cards or paper cutouts can be used. After matching, students read the rules aloud to practice speaking. In pairs, they talk about the rules they follow at school by making sentences such as ''I must arrive on time'' or ''I mustn’t skip lessons''. The teacher and peers provide feedback on accuracy, fluency, and active participation to make the activity engaging and effective. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity. Objective: To help students to describe school roles and responsibilities in English by using target vocabulary and to improve their speaking skills through active participation. Activity 2: Who Does What? The teacher prepares an activity with visuals representing school roles, such as a teacher and a cleaner, along with an information gap under each visual for their responsibilities, such as ''teaches lessons or cleans classrooms''. A word bank with the required words, such as ''teaches, cleans, manages, helps'', is provided at the top of the activity. Students actively fill in the blanks by using the correct words from the word bank (e.g., The teacher ___ lessons). After completing the gaps, they practise the sentences orally in pairs, using full sentences such as ''The teacher teaches lessons'', or ''The cleaner cleans classrooms''. The teacher and peers give feedback on their accuracy, fluency, and active participation to make the activity engaging and effective. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
